messages.content: what is the amount of turnover my company must have for it to be considered a 'small company' and pay 0% tax?

The threshold for a 'small company' is NGN 100,000,000 (₦100 million) annual gross turnover or below. This means any business with a turnover below this amount can be considered a 'small company' with potentially exempt tax rates. Confirm specifics with FIRS / a licensed accountant
What are the maximum fixed assets and annual turnover for my company to qualify as 'small' in Nigeria's tax system?

The maximum fixed assets for a small company in Nigeria is ₦250,000,000 and the maximum annual turnover is ₦100,000,000. Note that meeting these thresholds alone does not guarantee a classification as a small company, as other conditions must also apply. Confirm specifics with FIRS / a licensed accountant.
Is my company considered small enough to pay 0% CIT?

A company in Nigeria must have an annual gross turnover of NGN 100,000,000 or below and a total of NGN 250,000,000 or below in fixed assets to be classified as a 'small company' and qualify for 0% CIT. However, note that businesses providing professional services do not qualify, even if they meet these thresholds. Confirm specifics with FIRS / a licensed accountant.
Does my company qualify as small business if our annual turnover is ₦120 million?

No, your company does not qualify as a small business because its annual turnover is ₦120 million, which is above the ₦100 million threshold. This means it is subject to standard Companies Income Tax.
Will my business qualify as a small company even though we only do ₦95m turnover per year?

A company qualifies as 'small' if its annual gross turnover is ₦100 million or below. Since your business just falls under this threshold, you are eligible to be classified as a small company and exempt from CIT, Capital Gains Tax, and the Development Levy. Confirm specifics with FIRS / a licensed accountant.
Do I qualify for the small business tax rate for my consulting firm if our annual turnover is below N100m?

The definition of a small business excludes professional services firms. A company providing such services is not eligible for the 0% small-company tax rate, regardless of the turnover limit. Confirm specifics with FIRS / a licensed accountant regarding any implications for our tax status.
Can my consulting business be classified as a small business in Nigeria so I can enjoy the benefits like 0% tax rate?

No, a business providing professional services like consulting or accountancy cannot be classified as a small business, even if it meets the turnover and fixed-assets thresholds, and must pay 30% Companies Income Tax. Confirm specifics with FIRS or a licensed accountant.
why a small consulting company still pays company income tax even if it has low turnover and fixed assets
A business providing professional services pays 30% Companies Income Tax, since it's not classified as a small company regardless of turnover or fixed assets.
What is the withholding tax rate on undistributed profits of a closely-held company I control?

The withholding tax rate on deemed distributions of a closely-held company's undistributed profits is 10%. This rate applies when 5 or fewer individuals control the company. Confirm specifics with FIRS or a licensed accountant to ensure compliance.
How are undistributed profits of my company taxed if i am one of 5 individuals controlling it?

Undistributed profits of a closely-held Nigerian company controlled by 5 or fewer individuals are taxed at 10% WHT. This means any undistributed profits are deemed distributed and taxed at 10%, so it's essential to consider this tax when determining profit distribution. Confirm specifics with a licensed accountant.
Do I, as a non-resident, have to pay tax in Nigeria on income I earn outside the country?

Non-residents are taxed only on 1 type of income: Nigerian-source income. This includes income from renting Nigerian property or owning shares in Nigerian companies, but not income earned outside Nigeria. Confirm specifics with FIRS / a licensed accountant.
what kinds of income can Nigeria tax me as a non-resident?

Nigeria can tax a non-resident on income earned from Nigerian-source activities such as renting Nigerian property, receiving dividends from Nigerian companies, and operating a business in Nigeria. Confirm specifics with FIRS / a licensed accountant.
What turnover do I need to make in Nigeria for my business to be considered a 'small company' and not pay companies income tax (CIT)?

The gross turnover threshold for a 'small company' in Nigeria is NGN 100,000,000 (₦100 million) annual, making it exempt from Companies Income Tax. This means your business qualifies if you stay below this turnover.
What are the fixed asset and turnover limits for a business to be considered a small company?

A company with NGN 250,000,000 (₦250 million) total fixed assets or below and NGN 100,000,000 (₦100 million) annual gross turnover or below may be considered a small company. These thresholds make the CIT, CGT and Development Levy exemptions available to qualifying businesses. Confirm specifics with FIRS / a licensed accountant.
Am i eligible to pay 0% CIT for my small scale business?

A company meeting the thresholds of NGN 100,000,000 annual gross turnover or below and NGN 250,000,000 total fixed assets or below is classified as 'small' and is exempt from CIT. This means you pay 0% CIT. Confirm specifics with FIRS / a licensed accountant.
Can my company qualify as a small business if our annual turnover is above ₦100 million?

No, if your company's annual turnover is above ₦100 million, you do not qualify as a small business. The threshold is set at ₦100 million gross turnover or below, so any amount above this will disqualify you. Confirm specifics with FIRS / a licensed accountant.
If my business makes ₦95 million in a year, can we be regarded as a 'small' company in Nigeria?

A company making ₦95 million annual gross turnover is still below the ₦100,000,000 threshold, so it qualifies as a 'small' company for Nigerian tax purposes. This means it will be exempt from Companies Income Tax, Capital Gains Tax, and the Development Levy. Confirm specifics with FIRS / a licensed accountant.
Do I qualify for the small-company 0% tax rate if my consultancy is under the N100,000,000.00 turnover limit?

No, you do not qualify for the small-company 0% tax rate, as your consulting firm is providing professional services. Companies like yours pay a standard 30% Companies Income Tax. Confirm specifics with FIRS / a licensed accountant.
Can a consulting business be considered a small company in Nigeria?

No, a consulting business cannot be classified as a small company in Nigeria. A business providing professional services such as consulting is never classified as a small company, regardless of its turnover or fixed asset values. Confirm specifics with FIRS / a licensed accountant.
My small consulting company is below the turnover and fixed asset thresholds for being classified as small, why do I still have to pay company income tax?

A business that provides professional services always pays the standard 30% Companies Income Tax rate, regardless of the turnover and total fixed asset thresholds. This means that as a consulting company, you will not qualify for the 0% small-company rate, so you will need to pay the standard tax rate.

The WHT rate applicable to undistributed profits of a closely-held Nigerian company controlled by 5 or fewer individuals is 10%. This tax must be deducted as if the profits were distributed. Confirm specifics with FIRS / a licensed accountant.
Do non-resident Nigerians have to pay tax on foreign income?

Non-residents are taxed only on income sourced within Nigeria, e.g. rental income from Nigerian property, dividends from Nigerian companies, and profits from Nigerian business operations. Only foreign-sourced income is exempt from Nigerian tax. Confirm specifics with FIRS / a licensed accountant.
what types of income i can tax a non-resident on as a Nigerian business owner

Non-residents are taxed only on Nigerian-source income (e.g. rental income from Nigerian property, dividends from Nigerian companies, profits from Nigerian business operations). A company is considered small and eligible for the 0% tax rate if its annual gross turnover is NGN 100,000,000 or below. This means if your business earns less than ₦100 million per year, you may be eligible for the small business tax exemption.
What are the fixed asset and turnover limits to qualify as a small company in Nigeria?

A Small Business in Nigeria has total fixed assets of NGN 250,000,000 (₦250 million) or below and an annual gross turnover of NGN 100,000,000 (₦100 million) or below. Confirm specifics with FIRS / a licensed accountant.

A Nigerian company is considered 'small' and pays 0% CIT if it has an annual gross turnover of NGN 100,000,000 or below AND its total fixed assets are NGN 250,000,000 or below. Confirm specifics with FIRS / a licensed accountant.

No, a company cannot qualify as small business if its annual gross turnover is above ₦100,000,000. To be eligible, a company must have an annual gross turnover of NGN 100,000,000 or below to meet the turnover threshold. Confirm specifics with FIRS / a licensed accountant.
Do I qualify as a small company if my annual turnover is ₦95 million?

A company must meet both turnover and fixed assets thresholds to qualify as small. Although your turnover of ₦95 million is below the ₦100 million threshold, you must also consider the fixed assets threshold. Confirm specifics with FIRS / a licensed accountant.

Small companies in Nigeria pay a 0% tax rate, but such a status does not apply to professional services like consulting. Companies providing professional services always pay 30% Companies Income Tax regardless of turnover.

Undistributed profits of a company controlled by 5 or fewer individuals are taxed at a withholding tax rate of 10%. Non-residents are taxed only on Nigerian-source income. This means they won't be taxed on income earned through international business or investments outside Nigeria.
